text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Street vendors in the mining town of Ndola rioted to resist eviction from the main bus station.
- Tourism minister William Harrington says police recovered 320 miliary weapons and 1,770 muzzle loaders from 1,315 suspected poachers in the past eight months.
- Education minister Syamukayumba Syamujaye has told women that their affirmative action will not help them as they cannot "win against men".
- Copperbelt University chancellor Fwanyanga Mulikita has appealed to striking workers to resume work.
- A son of deputy chief justice Bonaventure Bweupe is facing charges of alleged aggravated robbery.
- Information Minister David Mpamba says the government will take up $400,000 in debt the state-run Times of Zambia owes South African suppliers.
